questions.question: Which epidemiological study design is most appropriate for studying the association between different doses of radiation exposure and the occurrence of multiple myeloma?
A research team identifies a group of 500 smokers and a group of 500 non-smokers. They follow both groups for 20 years to compare the rate of development of lung cancer. Which study design is this?
Which of the following epidemiological study designs does not include a control or comparison group?
In a prospective cohort study, 40% of the exposed group and 10% of the unexposed group are lost to follow-up. What type of bias might this introduce?
In a cohort study, exposure was measured by self-report. Some participants under-reported their intake of fatty diets. What is the type of bias?

An investigator aims to determine the extent to which the disease is attributable to the exposure in the studied group. Which of the following measures would be most appropriate for them to calculate from a cohort study?
Which of the following is a feature of a retrospective cohort?
questions.correct_answer: Both the exposure and outcome have already occurred before the study begins
wrong_answers: It starts with the outcome and looks back for exposures.
It starts with the exposure and follows subjects forward in time for the outcome.
The investigator manipulates the exposure of the diseased subjects.

questions.question: In a retrospective cohort study, what is the base to define the groups?
questions.correct_answer: Their past exposure status (exposed vs. unexposed).

questions.question: Which measure of association is calculated in a retrospective cohort study?

A study is conducted in which mothers are categorized based on their intake of sulfonamides during the first trimester of pregnancy (intake vs. no intake). At the time of delivery, the presence of heart defects in their newborns was evaluated. Which of the following metrics is used to determine the risk associated with sulfonamide intake and heart defects among newborns?

The association between low birth weight and maternal smoking during pregnancy can be studied by obtaining smoking history from women at the time of the first prenatal visit and then correlating birth weight (outcome) with smoking history (exposure). What type of study is this?

In 2025, a researcher uses hospital employment records from 1990 to classify workers as either exposed or unexposed to benzene. Then he reviews medical records from 1990 to 2025 to identify which workers developed leukaemia. No new participants are recruited. What is the study design?
In a case control study to reveal the causal association between cancer prostate & exposure to radiation, which of the following measures could be obtained?
questions.correct_answer: The rate of exposure to radiation among patients compared to control
wrong_answers: The excess risk of prostate cancer among patients exposed to radiation

questions.question: What type of epidemiological study is used to assess prior hormonal treatment use among women with a rare vaginal cancer and women without cancer?
What is the type of bias in the case-control studies where cases are more likely to memorize and report an exposure than controls?

An investigator suspects that the use of acetaminophen during the first trimester of pregnancy may cause neural tube defects (NTDs). Knowing that the prevalence of NTDs in the general infant population is 1 per 1,000 births, which is considered a rare prevalence. Which of the following is the most appropriate study design to investigate this hypothesis?

In a case-control study to find the relation between smoking and lung cancer, cases were asked detailed questions about smoking, while controls were only asked a single yes/no question. What is the type of bias?
Studying the relation between smoking and lung cancer using cases from a public hospital and controls from the population. What type of bias could arise?
Researchers conduct a case-control study on smoking and lung cancer. They match cases and controls by age and sex. Which statement is TRUE?
questions.correct_answer: Matching on age and sex allows the study to assess their effect on lung cancer
wrong_answers: Matching guarantees that there is no confounding in the study
Matching on age and sex allows clearer estimation of smoking-lung cancer relationship
Matching introduces bias that cannot be corrected in the analysis

questions.question: Temporal relationship can be missed in which of the following studies?

A research team follows 1200 organ transplant recipients and a similar group of non-transplant patients at an outpatient clinic over 1 year to determine the rate of development of pneumonia. What is this type of study?
Which of the following studies would be suitable for identifying the causes of a rare type of sarcoma, given that the registry for this cancer is unfortunately incomplete?
In case-control studies, what is the primary purpose of matching?
questions.correct_answer: To reduce the influence of confounding variables
wrong_answers: To ensure the exposure is equally distributed among cases and controls
To improve the statistical significance of results

questions.question: What is the measure of association reported from a case-control study?
An investigator wanted to study the relation between rare Hematologic Disorders in young infants & mothers smoking during pregnancy. Which is the best study design?
